title: Markets: Friday 30 October

morning.session_note: Weekday ASX edition · before the 10:00 open
summary: Alphabet had its worst day since listing, falling about 13% and wiping roughly US$500 billion off its value ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/29/alphabet-google-microsoft-msft-shares-today-earnings.html)). The Nasdaq fell 1.4% and the S&P 500 0.3% (snapshot), although most US stocks rose ([The Age/AP](https://www.theage.com.au/business/markets/asx-set-to-edge-up-alphabet-s-plunge-weighs-down-wall-street-ecb-chief-lagarde-resigns-20261030-p619vp.html)). After the close Amazon fell after missing profit and advertising forecasts, and Intel on a weaker sales forecast ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/29/amazon-amzn-q3-earnings-report-2026.html), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/29/intel-intc-q3-earnings-report-2026-.html)).

For Australia, ASX futures point higher ([The Age/AP](https://www.theage.com.au/business/markets/asx-set-to-edge-up-alphabet-s-plunge-weighs-down-wall-street-ecb-chief-lagarde-resigns-20261030-p619vp.html), [AFR](https://www.afr.com/markets/equity-markets/asx-to-rise-alphabet-plunges-13pc-amazon-to-report-20261030-p619vm)). Import prices fell 1.1% in the September quarter as fuel eased ([ABS](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/economy/price-indexes-and-inflation/international-trade-price-indexes-australia/latest-release)), and ASX futures put an 80% chance on an RBA hike on Tuesday at Thursday's close ([RBA Watch](https://rbawatch.com/rba-meeting/november-2026)).

Next: Australian PPI and private credit at 11:30am, Coles' first-quarter sales today, and the Bank of Japan at about 1:30pm ([Kinzan](https://kinzan.io/calendar/2026-10-30/), [Coles](https://www.colesgroup.com.au/investors/)). Iran says it has received a US letter proposing talks but has not replied ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/vance-outreach-to-iran-related-to-medical-supplies-says-trump-4984652)).

cards.headline: Alphabet has its worst day ever and drags the Nasdaq lower
cards.takeaway: Negative free cash flow and weaker search revenue sent Alphabet down about 13%, while most other US stocks rose.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Thursday's issue reported Alphabet's results and a fall of more than 7% after hours. New: Thursday's full session, the record fall and the wider market reaction.
cards.what_happened: Alphabet fell about 13%, its biggest drop since listing in 2004, beating the 11.63% record from March 2020 and wiping out roughly US$500 billion of market value. It reported negative free cash flow of US$9.07 billion against the US$2.7 billion analysts expected, kept 2026 capital spending guidance at US$195–205 billion, and search revenue of US$63.35 billion missed forecasts ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/29/alphabet-google-microsoft-msft-shares-today-earnings.html)). The report underscored worries about whether its heavy AI investment will pay off. Without Alphabet the S&P 500 would have risen; Eli Lilly, Mastercard, Merck and KLA all gained after results ([The Age/AP](https://www.theage.com.au/business/markets/asx-set-to-edge-up-alphabet-s-plunge-weighs-down-wall-street-ecb-chief-lagarde-resigns-20261030-p619vp.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: The fall was concentrated in large technology stocks: the semiconductor index fell 2.1% ([AFR](https://www.afr.com/markets/equity-markets/asx-to-rise-alphabet-plunges-13pc-amazon-to-report-20261030-p619vm)), while the Russell 2000 rose 0.8% in Reuters' afternoon report ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/wall-street-slides-as-alphabet-revenue-miss-revives-ai-capex-jitters-4984885)).
cards.market_reaction: S&P 500 −0.3% and Nasdaq −1.4% (snapshot). The Dow fell 132.54 points to 52,342.56 (The Age/AP).
cards.what_to_watch: Whether Amazon's and Intel's after-hours falls deepen the tech sell-off on Friday in the US.

competing_views.view: Alphabet had a messy set of results and a poorly handled call, and has lost its edge with Gemini.
Not a sea change; Alphabet's 4 billion search users put it in an enviable position as they become AI users.

cards.headline: Amazon and Intel fall after hours on their results
cards.takeaway: Amazon missed on profit and advertising while its sales guidance was in line; Intel beat on earnings but forecast lower sales than expected.
cards.key_figure: After hours: Amazon down more than 7% (CNBC) to more than 9% (Yahoo Finance) · Intel down 16% (CNBC)
cards.new_since_last_issue: New: both companies reported after Thursday's US close.
cards.what_happened: Amazon earned US$1.89 a share against US$1.96 expected (LSEG) and revenue of US$201.94 billion against US$202.31 billion. AWS revenue rose 39.3% to US$45.98 billion, but advertising of US$19.64 billion missed the US$20.82 billion expected. Fourth-quarter sales guidance of US$240–247 billion brackets the US$244.5 billion expected, and 2026 capital spending stays at US$220 billion ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/29/amazon-amzn-q3-earnings-report-2026.html), [Amazon](https://ir.aboutamazon.com/news-release/news-release-details/2026/Amazon-com-Announces-Third-Quarter-Results/default.aspx)). Intel earned 52 US cents a share against 40 cents expected, but guided fourth-quarter revenue to US$15–16 billion against US$17.1 billion expected (LSEG). CFO David Zinsner said the PC slowdown would continue at least through the first half of next year ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/29/intel-intc-q3-earnings-report-2026-.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: Both are large AI spenders reporting a day after Alphabet. Amazon's cloud revenue grew 39.3% while advertising missed. Intel's data centre and AI revenue rose 78% while its PC business shrank 5%; Counterpoint attributed weaker PC demand to higher memory costs (CNBC).
cards.market_reaction: Amazon fell more than 7% after hours according to CNBC and more than 9% according to Yahoo Finance's live coverage; the figures were taken at different times. Intel fell 16% (CNBC).
cards.what_to_watch: Friday's US session, and AMD's results next week (CNBC).

cards.headline: US growth beats forecasts while inflation stays well above target
cards.takeaway: The economy grew 3.4% annualised in the September quarter and core PCE inflation held at 3.1% a year.
cards.key_figure: GDP 3.4% annualised · core PCE 3.1% y/y · US 10Y 4.98% (−7 bp)
cards.new_since_last_issue: Thursday's issue listed these releases as upcoming. New: the results.
cards.what_happened: Real GDP grew at a 3.4% annual rate in the September quarter, up from 2.2% in the June quarter, and real final sales to private domestic purchasers rose 4.9% ([BEA](https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/gdp-advance-estimate-3rd-quarter-2026)). In September the PCE price index rose 0.5% for the month and 3.6% for the year; core PCE rose 0.3% and 3.1%. Personal income rose 0.2%, spending rose 0.5% and the saving rate was 3.8% ([BEA](https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/personal-income-and-outlays-september-2026)).
cards.why_it_matters: The inflation rise was driven largely by a surge in energy costs, with energy goods prices up 9.2% in the month, according to CNBC ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/29/pce-inflation-report-september-2026-.html)). CME FedWatch put the chance of a December Fed hike at 79.6% on Thursday, down from 84.2% on Wednesday ([IBTimes](https://www.ibtimes.com/septembers-inflation-was-line-expectations-odds-rate-hike-dropped-remain-high-3809143)).
cards.market_reaction: The US 10-year Treasury yield fell 7 bp to 4.98% and the 2-year fell 6 bp to 4.61% (snapshot, Treasury par curve).
cards.what_to_watch: The US employment cost index at 11:30pm tonight Sydney time.

comparison.title: Did US GDP beat a 3.1% or a 3.2% forecast?
comparison.why_different: The actual figure is the same everywhere (3.4%). The outlets used different surveys of economists: CNBC cites a Dow Jones consensus of 3.1%, while investinglive and the Kinzan calendar used 3.2%. Either way growth beat forecasts.

cards.headline: Oil edges lower on US–Iran diplomacy and an EU reserve release
cards.takeaway: Brent slipped 0.4% as the US reached out to Iran and the EU released reserves, while Houthi attacks and the risk of US strikes after the midterms limited the fall.
cards.key_figure: Gold futures −0.4% to US$4,036.7 · Brent: see comparison below
cards.new_since_last_issue: Thursday's issue covered Wednesday's rise on a US stock draw and the Houthi attack claim. New: Thursday's fall, the EU reserve release and the Vance letter (see the Iran card).
cards.what_happened: December ICE Brent settled at US$114.88, down 0.38%, after touching US$112.89, and WTI settled at US$102.00, down 0.76%, after briefly dropping below US$100 ([DTN](https://www.dtnpf.com/agriculture/web/ag/news/world-policy/article/2026/10/29/wti-stays-100-amid-mid-east-eu-fuel), [Reuters via Euronext](https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/oil-prices-settles-lower-diplomacy-hopes-offset-some-mideast-supply-concerns)). The EU authorised the release of 42 million barrels from strategic reserves, 21 million of them diesel ([DTN](https://www.dtnpf.com/agriculture/web/ag/news/world-policy/article/2026/10/29/wti-stays-100-amid-mid-east-eu-fuel)). Reports of new Houthi attacks on Saudi Aramco helped prices recover some losses later in the session, according to Reuters.
cards.why_it_matters: Import prices show the oil shock is starting to ease for Australia: petroleum import prices fell 8.7% in the September quarter, though they are still 48% higher than a year ago ([ABS](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/economy/price-indexes-and-inflation/international-trade-price-indexes-australia/latest-release)).
cards.market_reaction: Gold futures fell 0.4% to US$4,036.7 (snapshot, delayed). The snapshot's Brent futures change is not usable today; see the comparison.
cards.what_to_watch: The OPEC+ meeting on Sunday 1 November and Iran's reply to the US letter.

competing_views.view: "Oil prices are under pressure today amid renewed diplomatic efforts to de-escalate the conflict in the Middle East."
The interception of another Houthi missile "shows that threats to regional infrastructure remain active despite the renewed push for negotiations."
"There could be a geopolitical resolution right around the corner," which would ease inflation pressure.

comparison.title: Did Brent fall 0.4% or 3.1% on Thursday?
comparison.why_different: Different contracts and dates. December Brent settled at US$114.88, down 0.38% (DTN, Reuters). The snapshot's continuous series (Yahoo BZ=F) appears to have rolled to the January contract and compares it with December's Wednesday settle of US$115.32, so its −3.1% looks like a contract-roll artefact rather than a market move. The FRED spot series is an EIA assessment published with a lag (latest 27 Oct). The figures are not averaged; the settle is the one used in the text.

cards.headline: ASX set to edge higher despite the US tech sell-off
cards.takeaway: Futures point to a gain after Thursday's 0.5% rise, as the ASX has few large tech stocks exposed to Alphabet's fall.
cards.new_since_last_issue: New: Friday's opening indication and the Thursday close.
cards.what_happened: The ASX 200 closed up 0.5% at 8,891.8 on Thursday (snapshot), led by financials (+1.9%) and real estate (+1.8%), while consumer discretionary fell 2.0% ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/evening-wrap-asx-200-rises-as-flight-to-safety-lifts-banks-and-telcos-miners)). Futures pointed higher at the open on Friday: up 32 points or 0.4% at 6.59am AEDT according to The Age/AP, and up 15 points or 0.2% near 6am according to the AFR ([The Age/AP](https://www.theage.com.au/business/markets/asx-set-to-edge-up-alphabet-s-plunge-weighs-down-wall-street-ecb-chief-lagarde-resigns-20261030-p619vp.html), [AFR](https://www.afr.com/markets/equity-markets/asx-to-rise-alphabet-plunges-13pc-amazon-to-report-20261030-p619vm)).
cards.why_it_matters: The AFR described the local market as insulated from the Wall Street tech sell-off, since the ASX has few large technology stocks.
cards.market_reaction: Futures figures as reported by The Age/AP and AFR at different times; no futures level in today's snapshot.
cards.what_to_watch: Coles' first-quarter sales results today and the RBA decision at 2:30pm on Tuesday ([Coles](https://www.colesgroup.com.au/investors/)).

cards.headline: Import prices fall as fuel and fertiliser costs ease
cards.takeaway: Import prices fell for the first time since the September 2025 quarter, as fuel and fertiliser costs eased.
cards.key_figure: Import prices −1.1% q/q, +5.5% y/y · export prices +1.4% q/q (ABS)
cards.new_since_last_issue: Thursday's issue listed this release as upcoming. New: the result.
cards.what_happened: The import price index fell 1.1% in the September quarter after rising 5.7% in the June quarter, and is up 5.5% over the year. Petroleum products fell 8.7% and fertilisers 20.2% as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz gradually reopened, while computer equipment rose 7.3% on data centre demand. Export prices rose 1.4%, led by a 28.6% jump in gas prices ([ABS](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/economy/price-indexes-and-inflation/international-trade-price-indexes-australia/latest-release)).
cards.why_it_matters: This week's September-quarter CPI showed trimmed mean inflation of 1.0% q/q and headline inflation of 4.3% a year (AAP). Import prices are one input to consumer prices; the RBA decides on Tuesday.
cards.what_to_watch: The September-quarter producer price index (PPI) at 11:30am today; Kinzan's forecast is 1.0% q/q after 1.3% ([Kinzan](https://kinzan.io/calendar/2026-10-30/)).

cards.headline: Markets still put about 80% odds on an RBA hike next Tuesday
cards.takeaway: Pricing slipped slightly on Thursday but a hike to 4.85% remains the clear expectation.
cards.key_figure: Hike odds 80% at Thursday close (ASX futures via RBA Watch) · cash rate 4.60%
cards.new_since_last_issue: Thursday's close issue had 81% in the afternoon. New: the official Thursday close reading and Friday-morning pricing.
cards.what_happened: ASX 30-day interbank futures implied an 80% chance of a 25 bp hike at Thursday's close (expected rate 4.80%), from 82% on Wednesday. The live page showed 83% on Friday morning, and prediction markets 86% ([RBA Watch](https://rbawatch.com/rba-meeting/november-2026)).
cards.why_it_matters: A hike would be the fifth this year (AAP), and comes with new forecasts in the Statement on Monetary Policy. Market Index said pricing for a hike to 4.85% by year-end reached 100% on Thursday ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/evening-wrap-asx-200-rises-as-flight-to-safety-lifts-banks-and-telcos-miners)).
cards.market_reaction: Not separately observed; AU bond yields in today's data are lagged (21 Oct).
cards.what_to_watch: PPI at 11:30am today and the RBA decision at 2:30pm Tuesday 3 November, Melbourne Cup day.

cards.headline: ECB holds rates as Lagarde says she will leave early
cards.takeaway: The ECB debated a hike before holding, and Lagarde will step down in February, nine months before her term ends.
cards.new_since_last_issue: New: the decision and Lagarde's announcement.
cards.what_happened: The ECB kept its deposit rate at 2.50%, its main refinancing rate at 2.65% and its lending rate at 2.90% ([ECB](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/press_conference/monetary-policy-statement/2026/html/ecb.is261029~5c5ffe99e5.en.html)). Lagarde said the Governing Council debated whether a hike was appropriate and the decision was unanimous, and that unless there was a major development "the direction of travel is quite clear". She will step down on 7 February 2027, citing "freedom of speech, the freedom of expression" ([ECB](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/press_conference/monetary-policy-statement/2026/html/ecb.is261029~5c5ffe99e5.en.html), [Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/29/ecb-holds-rates-at-25-as-lagarde-announces-early-exit-with-inflation-near-double-the-targe)).
cards.why_it_matters: Euro-area inflation is 3.8% ([Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/29/ecb-holds-rates-at-25-as-lagarde-announces-early-exit-with-inflation-near-double-the-targe)). Money markets priced a 67% chance of a December ECB hike, according to LSEG data cited by CNBC ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/29/european-central-bank-interest-rates.html)).
cards.what_to_watch: Euro-area flash GDP at 9pm tonight Sydney time ([Kinzan](https://kinzan.io/calendar/2026-10-30/)).

competing_views.view: Expects one more hike, to 2.75%, in December.

competing_views.who: Dean Turner, UBS Global Wealth Management
competing_views.view: Described the decision as a "hawkish pause".

cards.headline: Bank of Japan expected to hold at 1.25% today
cards.takeaway: Economists expect a hold, with attention on whether the BoJ signals a December or January hike.
cards.key_figure: Policy rate 1.25%; decision about 1:30pm Sydney time
cards.new_since_last_issue: Thursday's issue listed the time. New: economists' expectations.
cards.what_happened: All 16 economists in a CNBC survey expect the BoJ to keep its policy rate at 1.25%, and all expect a hike in December or January ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/27/boj-october-meeting-rate-cnbc-survey.html)). The BoJ is likely to signal that underlying inflation has roughly reached its 2% target, according to Reuters ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/bank-of-japans-hawkish-pause-to-leave-scope-for-december-hike-4971365)). Markets price an 80% chance of a 25 bp hike in December, according to ING ([ING](https://think.ing.com/articles/boj-preview-hawkish-hold/)).
cards.why_it_matters: A move or a strong signal towards a December hike would affect the yen and global bond yields, which feed into Australian borrowing costs.
cards.what_to_watch: The decision and Outlook Report at about 1:30pm, and Governor Ueda's press conference at about 4:30pm ([Kinzan](https://kinzan.io/calendar/2026-10-30/)).

competing_views.view: Expect a rise to 1.5% in December.
The next hike is likely in January, when the BoJ releases its quarterly outlook report.

cards.headline: Iran confirms it received a US letter proposing talks but has not replied
cards.takeaway: Iranian media say any talks must meet seven conditions, while US officials say talks would need to cover the nuclear issue; the US midterms are on 3 November.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Thursday's close issue reported the Wall Street Journal's account of the Vance letter and Iran's openness to diplomacy. New: Iran's confirmation that it received the letter, its stated conditions, US officials' account of the terms, and Trump's comments.
cards.what_happened: Vance wrote to Mohsen Rezaei, head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, proposing direct talks. The New York Times reported it was passed through Qatari mediators on Sunday, as reported by Al Jazeera ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/29/what-we-know-of-vances-letter-to-rezaei-as-trump-warns-gulf-to-prepare)). A US official told Axios that talks "require discussions on the nuclear issue" and that "the President was enthusiastic about the letter" ([Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/10/28/vance-iran-nuclear-talks-letter)). Iran's Tasnim news agency said Iran had received the letter but had not responded, and that any talks must meet seven conditions, saying "any position that contradicts this framework is unacceptable". Asked whether he directed the letter, Trump said "No" and referred to medical supplies, according to Reuters ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/vance-outreach-to-iran-related-to-medical-supplies-says-trump-4984652)).
cards.why_it_matters: Oil is the main channel to Australia through fuel prices and inflation. Brent moved on reports about the diplomacy on Thursday (see the oil card).
cards.market_reaction: Brent edged lower on diplomacy hopes (see the oil card).
cards.what_to_watch: Iran's formal reply and the US midterms on 3 November.

competing_views.view: The risk of US strikes is "dangerously high" after the midterms.
"The President was enthusiastic about the letter," and talks "require discussions on the nuclear issue".
"Any position that contradicts this framework is unacceptable," referring to Iran's seven conditions.

rba.summary: ASX 30-day interbank futures put an 80% chance on a 25 bp hike on 3 November at Thursday's close (expected rate 4.80%), down from 82% on Wednesday. The live page showed 83% and prediction markets (Polymarket and Kalshi, as compiled by RBA Watch) 86% when checked on Friday morning.

forecasts.view: All four expect a hike on 3 November.

fed.summary: CME FedWatch put a 79.6% chance on a December hike on Thursday after the GDP and PCE data, down from 84.2% on Wednesday, as reported by IBTimes.

Consumer discretionary was the weakest sector, down 2.0%, on retailer trading updates and rate-hike concerns ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/evening-wrap-asx-200-rises-as-flight-to-safety-lifts-banks-and-telcos-miners)). Flight Centre made no announcement.

Up 0.9% to A$2.22 on Thursday (snapshot) on volume of 1.89 million shares, against 0.89 million on Wednesday (IDP investor site). IDP filed final interest notices for departing directors A Barker and A Barkla and a buy-back update on 29 October. No specific driver for the move was reported.

close.session_note: Weekday ASX edition · after the close
summary: The ASX 200 rose 0.2% to 8,908.1, well off a morning high of 8,992.7, and gained 1.3% for the week. Consumer discretionary rebounded 2.6% and industrials 1.3%, while Coles fell 7.6% after warning first-half supermarket earnings would be flat and tech fell 1.3% as the US AI sell-off spread ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/asx-200-live-today-friday-30th-october), [AAP](https://aapnews.aap.com.au/news/aussie-shares-track-strong-weekly-finish-coles-tumbles)).

ASX 30-day futures put the chance of a 3 November RBA hike at 79%, against 80% at Thursday's close. Producer prices rose 1.1% in the September quarter and 3.6% over the year, a touch above the 1.0% forecast. The Bank of Japan held at 1.25% with one dissent for a hike ([RBA Watch](https://rbawatch.com/rba-meeting/november-2026), [ABS](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/economy/price-indexes-and-inflation/producer-price-indexes-australia/latest-release), [Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/boj-keeps-interest-rates-steady-signals-further-rate-hikes-4985752)).

Asian chip stocks fell after Amazon and Intel results, with the KOSPI down more than 3% late in the session. December Brent rose 1.2% to US$116.24 after Houthi attacks on Saudi sites, and Iran said it had not answered a US letter. cards.headline: ASX 200 ends a strong week higher, but well off its morning peak
cards.takeaway: Retailers and industrials rebounded while Coles, tech and miners dragged as the US AI sell-off reached Asia.
cards.new_since_last_issue: This morning's briefing expected a higher open, which came: the index was up as much as 1.1% (Market Index) before giving back most of the gain in the afternoon.
cards.what_happened: The S&P/ASX 200 closed at 8,908.1, up 16.3 points or 0.18%, after reaching 8,992.7 in the morning (close snapshot; Yahoo Finance day range). It rose 1.28% for the week, and financials have gained more than 8% over three straight weekly rises ([AAP](https://aapnews.aap.com.au/news/aussie-shares-track-strong-weekly-finish-coles-tumbles)). Consumer discretionary rose 2.6%, industrials 1.3%, energy 1.1%, health care 0.8% and utilities 0.8%. Tech fell 1.3%, materials 1.0% and staples 0.9% (S&P/ASX sector indices, Yahoo Finance, late trade). Market Index said the market stayed defensive, with most defensive sectors outside staples higher, and that non-energy miners were on track for their first weekly gain in nine weeks ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/asx-200-live-today-friday-30th-october)).
cards.why_it_matters: The AFR said the market pared gains in the afternoon as the Wall Street tech sell-off hit local sentiment ([AFR](https://www.afr.com/markets/equity-markets/asx-to-rise-alphabet-plunges-13pc-amazon-to-report-20261030-p619vm)). Market Index noted discretionary was still down 2.4% for the week after weak trading updates, and that bank results are due next week: Westpac on Monday, NAB on Thursday and Macquarie on Friday.
cards.what_to_watch: Westpac's results on Monday and the RBA decision at 2:30pm on Tuesday.

cards.headline: Coles falls 7.6% on a flat earnings warning; Reece and JB Hi-Fi rise
cards.takeaway: Quarterly updates drove the biggest moves, with Coles, Catalyst Metals and lithium names down and Reece and retailers up.
cards.what_happened: **Coles (COL) −7.6% to A$21.68**, after falling more than 12% in the morning. It expects first-half Supermarkets EBIT to be flat at about A$1.23 billion, against A$1.32 billion expected, and supermarket comparable sales growth slowed to 2.7% from 4.6% a year earlier. It cited price investment, competitor promotions and fuel costs, and is relaunching its Every Day Price program ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/asx-200-live-today-friday-30th-october)). **Reece (REH) +9.4% to A$17.25** after first-quarter sales rose 4.3% to A$2.5 billion ([AAP](https://aapnews.aap.com.au/news/aussie-shares-track-strong-weekly-finish-coles-tumbles)). **JB Hi-Fi (JBH) +5.7%, Endeavour (EDV) +4.9%, James Hardie (JHX) +4.0% and Wesfarmers (WES) +3.2%** as retailers recovered part of the week's losses. Macquarie kept an outperform rating on JB Hi-Fi with an A$87 target, and Endeavour's sales rose 2.8% to A$3.18 billion (Market Index). **Catalyst Metals (CYL) −24.8%** after quarterly gold output fell 30% to 22,200 ounces and it set FY27 guidance of 90,000–105,000 ounces (Market Index). **Lithium:** Vulcan fell 13.7%, Liontown 6.4% and PLS 4.4% as Chinese lithium carbonate futures fell again, according to Market Index. Rio Tinto fell 1.8% after pausing underground mining at Oyu Tolgoi following a seismic event that injured three workers ([Rio Tinto](https://www.riotinto.com/en/news/releases/2026/seismic-event-at-oyu-tolgoi)). DXN fell 47.2% after its first US AI customer said it intends to cancel an A$8.8 million contract (Market Index). Closing prices and changes are from Yahoo Finance.
cards.why_it_matters: Market Index said Coles had been on track for its worst session on record when it was down more than 12%. Woolworths rose 2.0% (Yahoo Finance). The AFR reported the federal government plans to ban AI data centres near homes.

sections.note: Asian markets were still trading at the close snapshot. Tokyo and Seoul close at 5:30pm Sydney time, Shanghai at 6pm and Hong Kong at 7pm, so these tiles show late-session prices, not closes.

cards.headline: Asian chip stocks slide after Amazon and Intel; BOJ holds
cards.takeaway: Seoul, Taipei and Tokyo fell on AI spending worries while Hong Kong rose; the BOJ held but signalled more hikes.
cards.new_since_last_issue: The Asian sell-off and the BOJ decision are new since this morning's briefing.
cards.what_happened: Late in their sessions the KOSPI was down 3.3% and the Nikkei 225 2.1%, while the Hang Seng was up 1.9% and Shanghai 0.1% (close snapshot, Yahoo Finance). The Korea Times reported the KOSPI down more than 5% late in the morning, and Reuters said the KOSPI's fall for October was nearly 16%. Pepperstone's Chris Weston said the market was "increasingly questioning whether shareholders will earn an adequate return on the enormous capital being deployed" ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/stocks-slump-bonds-leap-as-ai-giants-spending-spooks-investors-4985741)). The Bank of Japan held its rate at 1.25% by an 8–1 vote, with Hajime Takata proposing a rise to 1.5%. It said underlying inflation was broadly consistent with its 2% target, raised its core inflation forecast for the year to March 2028 to 2.6% from 2.4%, and will speed up its ETF sales from January ([CNA/Reuters](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/boj-keeps-interest-rates-steady-signals-further-rate-hikes-6505836)).
cards.why_it_matters: Most analysts polled by Reuters expect a BOJ hike to 1.5% in December, according to CNA. Governor Ueda speaks at 5:30pm Sydney time. Bitcoin hit a six-week low after a suspected hack at Binance before trading near US$78,200, according to Reuters.

cards.headline: RBA hike odds steady near 80% as producer prices rise 1.1%
cards.takeaway: The September-quarter PPI came in slightly above forecast, and futures still lean strongly to a hike on Tuesday.
cards.key_figure: Nov hike odds 79% (ASX futures, 30 Oct afternoon)
cards.new_since_last_issue: This morning's briefing had 80% at Thursday's close and the PPI still to come. Both are updated here.
cards.what_happened: ASX 30-day interbank futures implied a 79% chance of a 25 bp hike to 4.85% on 3 November when we checked at about 4:25pm, against 80% at Thursday's close; prediction markets had 87% ([RBA Watch](https://rbawatch.com/rba-meeting/november-2026)). Final-demand producer prices rose 1.1% in the September quarter and 3.6% over the year, after 1.3% in June. Building construction rose 1.3% and services rose with the minimum-wage increase, while manufacturing output prices fell 1.3%, led by a 13.2% drop for petroleum and coal products ([ABS](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/economy/price-indexes-and-inflation/producer-price-indexes-australia/latest-release)). Kinzan's calendar forecast was 1.0% ([Kinzan](https://kinzan.io/calendar/2026-10-30/)). The Australian dollar was at US$0.7038, down 0.3%, late in the day (close snapshot); AAP had 70.40 US cents.
cards.why_it_matters: The decision and new forecasts are at 2:30pm on Tuesday. No same-day closing Australian bond yields were available; the dashboard tiles show the RBA's table, last updated for 28 October. We did not find a verified report on today's private credit figures.

cards.headline: Brent rises on Houthi attacks as Iran holds off on a US letter
cards.takeaway: Oil edged up on supply worries, heading for a fourth monthly gain, while gold and copper eased.
cards.new_since_last_issue: This morning's briefing had the December contract settling at US$114.88 and the Vance letter. Today's rise and the Houthi attacks are new.
cards.what_happened: The December Brent contract, which expires today, was at US$116.24 a barrel at 3:49pm Sydney time, up 1.2% from Thursday's settlement; the January contract was up 1.0% at US$111.94 (Yahoo Finance). Yemen's Houthis said they had attacked several Saudi sites, including the Ras Tanura refinery, and Iran's Revolutionary Guards said three tankers hit sea mines south of the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Tasnim agency said Tehran had received a letter from US Vice President JD Vance but not replied, according to Reuters ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/30/oil-rises-on-supply-concerns-as-houthis-attack-saudi-arabia.html)). Gold futures were at US$4,010.20 an ounce, down 0.5%, and COMEX copper at US$6.560 a pound, down 0.3% (close snapshot). Iron ore was unchanged at US$90.71 a tonne at its latest settle.
cards.why_it_matters: Brent is on course for a gain of nearly 14% in October, according to CNBC. Energy rose 1.1% on the ASX, with Woodside up 1.9% and Santos 1.4% (Yahoo Finance).

cards.headline: Euro-area GDP at 9pm and US wage costs at 11:30pm
cards.takeaway: Data and the US tech sell-off set the tone into the weekend, with China's PMIs on Saturday and OPEC+ on Sunday.
cards.what_happened: Euro-area flash September-quarter GDP and unemployment are due at 9pm Sydney time, and the US employment cost index at 11:30pm; Kinzan's forecasts are 0.2% for GDP and 0.8% for the ECI. The US cash market opens at 12:30am ([Kinzan](https://kinzan.io/calendar/2026-10-30/)). Nasdaq 100 futures were down 1.9% in Asian trade after Amazon fell 7% and Intel 23% in extended trading, according to Reuters.
cards.why_it_matters: China's official PMIs are due at 12:30pm Saturday ([Kinzan](https://kinzan.io/calendar/2026-10-31/)), and seven OPEC+ countries meet on output on Sunday ([OPEC](https://www.opec.org/pr-detail/616-4-october-2026.html)).
cards.what_to_watch: Euro-area GDP at 9pm, the US ECI at 11:30pm and the US open at 12:30am, Sydney time.

cards.headline: Open for the weekend and Monday's briefing
cards.takeaway: The US tech sell-off, the RBA, bank results, Iran and OPEC+ remain open.
cards.what_happened: **US:** whether Amazon's and Intel's falls carry into tonight's session after Alphabet's record drop (Reuters). **RBA:** 79% hike pricing for 2:30pm Tuesday ([RBA Watch](https://rbawatch.com/rba-meeting/november-2026)). **Banks:** Westpac reports Monday, NAB Thursday and Macquarie Friday (Market Index). **Middle East:** Iran's response to the Vance letter and Houthi attacks on Saudi sites ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/30/oil-rises-on-supply-concerns-as-houthis-attack-saudi-arabia.html)); OPEC+ meets Sunday. **Crypto:** the suspected Binance hack, which has frozen about US$3 billion of assets, according to Market Index.
cards.why_it_matters: Each could move the ASX open, rate expectations or oil on Monday.

rba.summary: About a 79% chance of a 25 bp hike on 3 November in ASX 30-day interbank futures on Friday afternoon, against 80% at Thursday's close.

watchlist.note: Down 3.0% to A$1.805, easing after Thursday's 6.6% jump and a rebound from A$1.46 on 23 October; it traded between A$1.77 and A$1.895. Morningstar today kept its A$3.50 fair value, saying investors are too pessimistic about the US fraud hit and higher US bad debts (1.93% of transaction value), while Zip has reaffirmed FY27 cash EBTDA guidance of A$340 million. The only new filing was a director's interest notice.

Up 1.4% to A$200.35 as health care rose 0.8% and investors favoured defensive sectors, according to Market Index. CSL had no price-sensitive news; its only filing was an update on its share buy-back, which is still running.
Up 0.4% to A$11.34 as consumer discretionary rebounded 2.6%. It traded as high as A$11.54 but lagged the sector's gain. Flight Centre has made no announcement since 20 October.
Down 0.5% to A$2.21 in a narrow A$2.195–2.24 range, missing the discretionary rebound. IDP updated its running share buy-back this morning and had no price-sensitive news.
